newsitem.title: GEORGIA: IMF mission happy with Georgia reforms.
newsitem.headline: IMF mission happy with Georgia reforms.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund (IMF) official on Monday praised the economic policy of the Georgian government.
"The overall assessment of the present economic situation is positive," Mohammad-Shadman Valavi told Reuters by telephone.
Valavi, winding up a routine IMF mission to Georgia, said that country's main macroeconomic indicators meet the demands of the organisation.
He singled out the stability of the national currency , the lari, balancing at around 1.3 to dollar, and low monthly inflation which is holding at about 1.2 percent.
At the same time Valavi said the IMF still wanted Georgia to improve tax collection.
"In spite of the increase in the tax revenues to eight percent of GDP (Gross Domestic Product) in 1996 (from two percent in 1994), this level remains very low," he said.
Valavi also said the pace of privatisation in Georgia was too slow. "The improvement of the investment climate depends on the pace of the privatisation," he added.
He said he thought the continued stability of the economy would aid in ensuring that foreign investment in the economy would continue.
Valavi said the next IMF visit was planed for the end of July.

"The second part of the $80 million ESAF credit will be allocated to the republic in September or October of this year after the visit in July," he said. $40 million has already been released to the government this year.
The 1997 ESAF loan package is part of a three-year $246 package, $80 million of which was disbursed in 1996.
